block.description: The `sym_environment` resource provides an Environment to deploy one or more Flows. You may use multiple Environments such as 'sandbox' and 'prod' to safely test your flows in isolation before deploying them for production usage.

destination.description: The destination channel to send error messages to.

integration_id.description: The ID for the Slack Integration associated with this error logger.

block.description: The `sym_error_logger` resource defines a Slack channel destination for error messages encountered while executing a Flow.

environment_id.description: The ID of the Environment this Flow is associated with.

implementation.description: Python code defining custom logic for the Flow.

label.description: An optional label for the Flow.

name.description: A unique identifier for the Flow.

vars.description:
A map of variables and their string values to pass to `impl.py`. Useful for making IDs generated dynamically by Terraform available to your `impl.py`.

~> **Note:** While you may pass in other primitives (e.g. bool, int) as a value to `sym_flow.vars`, they will be cast to strings when you apply your configuration. When accessing these values in your `impl.py`, you will need to recast them into the correct types before using them.

additional_header_text.description: Additional text to append to the header text displayed at the top of the Slack request modal, after the default header text. Supports Slack markdown.

allow_guest_interaction.description: Whether to allow guest users to interact with this sym_flow. If true, guest users can click the "Approve", "Deny", and "Revoke" buttons in Slack. If false, guest users' interactions with this sym_flow's requests will be rejected.'

allow_revoke.description: Whether access granted by a sym_strategy may be revoked before the requested duration is over. If true, shows a "Revoke" button in Slack that allows both the requester and approver to instantly revoke access. At least one of "schedule_deescalation" or "allow_revoke" must be true.

allowed_sources.description: A list of sources from which this sym_flow may be invoked. Valid sources are: "slack", "api". If unspecified, all sources will be enabled. If an empty list is specified, it will not be possible for this sym_flow to be invoked.

include_decision_message.description: Whether users responding to requests may enter additional text as context for their decisions. If true, shows an input box on all open requests.

schedule_deescalation.description: Whether automatic access de-escalation will occur after a requested duration. If false, de-escalation will only occur when manually revoked. At least one of "schedule_deescalation" or "allow_revoke" must be true.

strategy_id.description: The ID of a sym_strategy with sym_targets that this sym_flow will be managing access to. If not defined, this sym_flow will be approval-only.

allowed_values.description: Defines the full list of valid choices for this field's value. If defined, this field will be displayed as a dropdown in Slack. Not applicable for the "slack_user" and "slack_user_list" types.

default.description: A fallback value for optional fields if no value is provided. Not applicable for the "slack_user", "slack_user_list", "int_list", and "str_list" types.

label.description: A name for the field, to be displayed in Slack.

name.description: A unique identifier for this field.

on_change.description: Python code defining logic to execute when this field's value changes.

prefetch.description: Whether a prefetch reducer will be used to populate the options for this field. Not applicable for the "slack_user" and "slack_user_list" types.

required.description: Whether this field is a required input.

type.description: The type of data stored in this field. One of: "string", "str_list", "int", "int_list", "bool", "duration", "slack_user", "slack_user_list".

visible.description: Whether this field is rendered in the prompt modal.

block.description: Custom input field used to collect information from a user who is requesting access to a resource.
A set of parameters which configure the Flow.
The `sym_flow` resource defines an approval workflow in Sym, allowing users to request temporary and auto-expiring access to sensitive resources.

implementation.description: Python code defining the `get_flows` reducer for the FlowsFilter.

integrations.description: A map of Integrations available when executing this FlowsFilter's implementation.

vars.description: A map of variables and their values to pass to this FlowsFilter implementation.

block.description: The `sym_flows_filter` resource provides a FlowsFilter that can be used to filter the Flows displayed to the requester. You may only have one FlowsFilter resource in your organization.

settings.description: A map of settings specific to this type of Integration.

block.description: The `sym_integration` resource allows you to provide Sym with the credentials and context to connect to an external service. For example, a PagerDuty integration or a Slack integration.
